findings.reason: the plan should name node_probe as the owner the retention liveness probe extends, so a second un-timed scheduler query is not left beside the timed one.
findings.text: the §8 retention design ("the job id appears in no squeue state for the account", plan lines 571/579) is built as a second, unbounded scheduler query — subprocess.run(["squeue","-h","-o","%i","-u",...]) with no timeout and only a FileNotFoundError guard (default_running_job_ids, called at :733 and :877) — while node_probe.run_capture (imas_ambix/agent/node_probe.py:186, timeout_s=10.0) and node_probe.read_jobs (imas_ambix/agent/node_probe.py:667) already bound the call and tell a squeue that refused from a node that has none; a hung squeue here blocks the whole retire-raw listing; also registered against this section at c-20261005T1005-s8-plan-review and not answered in §8's text

findings.reason: the publisher and the §9 estimate writer should call one shared atomic-write owner rather than each carrying its own, which is the same duplicate the plan set out to remove from gpu-watch.
findings.text: the plan names provider_prices the owner of the price table and §12 fixes its atomic scratch-rename (write_atomic), yet the plan's §10 publisher adds a second atomic writer (imas_ambix/agent/watch_publish.py:74 _write_atomic) and two more scratch-renames already exist at imas_ambix/agent/lane.py:615, imas_ambix/agent/lane.py:1023 and imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:3557; the plan names no shared owner for atomic writes

findings.reason: name SiteConfig as the resolver for the published document so a relocation of the endpoint directory cannot split the two files apart.
findings.text: the plan's §10 revision fixes the published document at the literal ~/public/imas-ambix/watch.json (plan line 661) while the lane document it must sit beside is resolved through SiteConfig.endpoint_document.with_name("lane.json") (imas_ambix/agent/live_panel.py:529, profile.py:620 endpoint_document); the plan says "beside lane.json" but names no resolution owner

findings.reason: the section must account for the added CLI surface in its own text, since cli_options is 0 this week.
findings.text: the retention section adds agent retire-raw and its --apply flag, and the frozen-manifest apply flow, without stating in its text what it retires or merges or why nothing can be, unlike §5 (removes --submit/--dry-run), §11 (accounts for --live). Prior review c-20261005T1005-s8-plan-review raised exactly this against this section and the text does not answer it

findings.reason: the same accounting §11 gives for --live is owed for the publisher command it now depends on.
findings.text: the §10 revision renders gpu-watch's period ledger from a document published by a new command, agent publish-watch, adding a CLI command and a second published document (watch.json) whose interface surface is accounted for by no section's text; §10 names the document source but not what the new command retires or merges

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §11 hides the lane copy, the receipt tail and the two block shapes behind live_panel()/lane_block()/live_block() over about thirty private helpers (imas_ambix/agent/live_panel.py:434-533), and §2's TelemetryIndex hides ingest/rebuild/query behind one class; both are one module with a small interface over substantial behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan introduces three duplicates of shared infrastructure (a second scheduler query, a second atomic-write, and a second resolution of the published-document path) rather than extending the owners that already exist.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; two sections add CLI surface (retire-raw/--apply; publish-watch) whose text names neither what it retires or merges nor why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the machinery it extends and each citation was opened: counter_span and _prefix_hit_rate (§3), partitioned_total vs compact_rows (§8, imas_ambix/agent/telemetry_index.py:1464 rebuild, telemetry_store.compact_file), the lane document and its lane.py derivations (§11/§14, imas_ambix/agent/lane.py:651 availability_percent, :725 lane_headroom), and provider_prices (§12, imas_ambix/agent/provider_prices.py). §2's rebuild-equals-append requirement is already a test (tests/test_telemetry_index.py:355, :388). The two mechanisms it rebuilds without citing are reported under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two thin layers the plan adds each state why the existing machinery cannot absorb it: §11 says --live cannot merge into --json because its purpose is to skip the index, and §10 says gpu-watch consumes the JSON document rather than importing the package to stay a standalone script.
